html:
The Chehalis are a Coast Salish people of southwestern Washington, living along the Chehalis River and around Grays Harbor. They were divided into the Upper Chehalis inland and the Lower Chehalis near the coast.

They lived by salmon fishing, hunting and gathering roots and berries, and traded with the Chinook to the south, the Quinault on the coast and the Cowlitz to the east. In the 1850s they refused the treaty terms the United States offered, which would have moved them away from their river. A reservation was set up for them on the Chehalis River in 1864, and the Confederated Tribes of the Chehalis Reservation still live there.
